text:
anya: Heads-up — after rolling cilium 1.21 to canary on europe-west2-gpu yesterday we're seeing intermittent east-west packet loss and RDMA handshake failures for training pods. p99 latency for pod-to-pod up from ~2ms to 40-80ms in bursts.

miguel: Confirmed. Affected jobs are all-reduce RPCs; tcp retransmits + huge retry spikes. GPU jobs stall then recover.

oncall-bot: Incident created: I-20260318-41 — cilium-1.21-canary-eastwest-pktloss (sev: high)

ravi: Any MTU changes in the upgrade? Did the cni switch tunnel mode or enable GSO offload differently?

anya: We didn't intentionally change cluster MTU. Noted cilium's default geneve mtu patch got applied. Kernel logs show neighbour/gratuitous arp churn. Sending quick repro from a failing node: 

```
# iperf3 client -> pod
iperf3 -c 10.2.43.12 -P 8 -t 10
[SUM] 0.00-10.00 sec  9.45 GBytes  8.11 Gbits/sec  sender

# tracepath from pod -> pod
tracepath 10.2.43.12
 1: 10.2.43.1                                          1.273ms pmtu 1450
 2: 10.2.18.33                                        2.512ms
 3: 10.2.43.12                                        3.907ms

# dmesg shows repeated: cilium: skb: GSO failed, dropping packet
```

miguel: That GSO/GRO/GSO offload error screams MTU/tunnel offload mismatch. Were we using macvlan/host device for RDMA (ib0) and cilium accidentally started encapsulating ib0 traffic?

jules: We have direct RDMA (ib0) between the nodes for NVLink/GPUDirect tests. Cilium should be configured to exclude IB interfaces but the new canary added an extra device glob that may match `ib*`.

ravi: Can you run ethtool on ib0 & the tunnel? Quick checks:
```
ethtool -k ib0 | egrep "(gso|gro|ts)"
ethtool -k cilium_vxlan0
```

anya: Ran those. Output: 
```
# ib0
generic-segmentation-offload: on
generic-receive-offload: on
# cilium_geneve0
generic-segmentation-offload: off
generic-receive-offload: off
```

anya: So cilium disabled GSO on geneve but left ib0 with GSO on — when traffic crosses kernel path it gets fragmented/dropped. There's also an MTU mismatch: node's host dev MTU=9000, geneve pmtu=1450.

miguel: That explains the RDMA handshake failures — packets that should bypass encapsulation are being routed through the CNI path due to recent iptables rule reorder in 1.21.

infra-sre: Proposed mitigation: 1) Pause the 1.21 canary; 2) Pin canary nodes to 1.20; 3) Apply temporary iptables rule to bypass Cilium for ib0 traffic; 4) Collect tcpdump+skb logs for SRE and cilium team.

jules: We should avoid manual iptables changes unless short-lived. Quick rollback is safest to restore job SLOs. Can we cordon and drain canary nodes and revert daemonset?

anya: I can do an emergency rollback. Plan: drain the 3 canary nodes (eu-west2-gpu-canary-1..3), patch cilium daemonset to image 1.20.7, monitor packetloss and training job health.

ravi: Also capture `cilium monitor` output and `bpftool net` before drain in case we need to file upstream bug.

anya: Taking action now. Steps I'm running: 
```
kubectl cordon eu-west2-gpu-canary-1
kubectl drain eu-west2-gpu-canary-1 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
kubectl set image ds/cilium cilium-agent=cilium/cilium:v1.20.7 -n kube-system
```

anha (typo): ignore — accidental message, sorry :face_palm: 

miguel: :thumbsup: let us know when first node is back to 1.20 and any p99 numbers.

anya: First node reverted; p99 dropped back to ~3ms on that node's pods. Training tasks that were stuck resumed. Rolling the other two now.

infra-sre: Good call. Next steps for postmortem: 1) Add explicit device exclude for RDMA (`devices: "!ib*"`) in our cilium config; 2) Add e2e job that runs RDMA handshake test pre-rollout; 3) Reproduce locally with MTU mismatch and confirm GSO handling; 4) Open upstream bug for cilium's iptables reorder and GSO interaction.

jules: Also add a probe in Optimize that watches for sudden p99 east-west jumps tied to canary labels so rollouts auto-pause sooner.

anya: Filing follow-ups now. Will paste logs and cilium-monitor output to the incident ticket.

oncall-bot: Incident I-20260318-41 updated: mitigation in progress (rollback).

ravi: Thanks everyone. If possible, schedule a small canary with host-device exclusion and MTU validation before re-rolling 1.21.

anya: Agreed. I'll coordinate with release for a targeted patch release and add the preflight check to the rollout job.

miguel: Adding note for capacity planning: this caused ~12% effective GPU throughput loss for the region during the window; flagging for cost/comp impact in the postmortem.

anya: End of thread — will update incident with artifacts.
